MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  MAY 1, 2024
  CITY HALL - MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  5:00 RM.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Frost called the meeting t0 order at 5:05 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT:  Chair Chris Frost, Vice Chair Joshua Spiegel, Commissioners Brian
  Merrick, Keegan Gibbs, and Ex Officio Member Brent Woodworth.

  , ABSENT:  Commissioner Daphne Anneet

  ALSO PRESENT:  Susan Dueflas, Public Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works
  Director; Luis Flores, Public Safety Liaison; Sarah Flores, Emergency Services
  Coordinator; Gabe Etcheverry, Fire Safety Liaison; Travis Hart, Deputy Public Works
  Director; Sergeant Christopher Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff‘s Department, *
  Mark Russo Malibu VOP Team Leader, and Cynthia Alba, Executive Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Bill Melcher led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Executive Assistant Alba reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  April 25, 2024

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Gibbs moved and Commissioner Merrick seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The motion carried 4-0, with Commissioner Anneet absent.

ITEM l  CEREMONIAL / PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Moshe Ben Dayan from Tip Top Tow spoke about his services, he stated that he
  owns several tow companies throughout the Los Angeles County region. He
  stated that they received the contract for the Malibu Sheriff’s Department and
  stated that it is difficult to travel from Santa Monica. He requested a vehicle
  storage space to allow for a quicker response.

  Meril May spoke about traffic concems including keeping shoulders free of
  debris, clearing intersections of brush, clearing signs, angles to PCH, parking sign
  updates, road surfaces, keeping construction areas safe, f1re breaks, and speed
  feedback signs.

ITEM 2.B.  STAFF COMMENTS

  Public Safety Director Duenas provided an update about the fire policy discussed
  at the last meeting. She stated that she, alongside other city team members and
  experts from the community, is working on a campaign to change behavior on
  PCH to slow traffic down.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores provided an update on activity regarding
  homelessness throughout the city, an update on the K booster, and AFPR camera
  placements for the city.

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry stated that Fire Safety Liaison Brad Yocum guided
  Malibu West towards being a Firewise Community and commended him. He also
  stated that tree grant activities are active and invited the community to apply to
  remove hazardous trees.

  Emergency Services Coordinator Flores stated that city staff and CERT members
  have participated in EOC training. Provided an update on the Annual Safety and
  Preparedness Fair and added that there will be two upcoming Fire Extinguisher
  training courses at City Hall.

  Public Works Director DuBoux provided an update on public safety surrounding
  PCH, he stated that the Public Works Department is working closely with
  Caltrans on multiple proj ects.

  Deputy Public Works Director Hart stated that work had begun on the annual
  weed abatement and provided an update on the storm debris cleanup efforts,
  summer safety messages, and an update on the Topanga Canyon Closure.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission

ITEM 2.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  EX Officio Member Woodworth stated that he attended a conference in Reno,
  Nevada, and he stated that he will attend the Natural Hazards Conference in
  Boulder with the FEMA Director.

  Commissioner Merrick requested an update from Los Angeles County Beaches
  and Harbor regarding the Arizona Crossing opening.

  Chair Frost shared that parking at Point Dume has been challenging and stated
  that the state should be more involved. He also added that Winding Way has been
  another problem because people are running across PCH. He also spoke about the
  need for a city tow yard to speed up the towing process.

  Vice Chair Spiegel inquired for more information regarding the slide at
  Geoffrey’s.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated that he is working with the property owner
  and Caltrans to secure an encroachment permit in order to remove the debris.

  Vice Chair Spiegel inquired if anything could be done to speed up the process for
  the Topanga Canyon.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated that Caltrans is doing everything that they
  can and fully understands the importance of opening up the canyon as soon as
  possible.

  Public Safety Director Dueflas stated that she met with Fire Chief Smith and
  stated that the Los Angeles County Fire Department is working closely with the
  Topanga community.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Gibbs moved and Vice Chair Spiegel seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called and the motion carried 4-
  0, with Commissioner Anneet absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.

  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes  March 6, 2024
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes 0f May l, 2024
Page 4 of 9

  Staff recommendation: Approve minutes of the Public Safety Commission
  Regular meeting of March 6, 2024.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A. Fiscal Year (FY) 2024  2025 Recommended Assignments

  Recommended Action: 1) Review Public Safety Commission assignments from
  FY 2023-2024, remove completed assignments, and add new topics for
  consideration, and 2) Provide a recommendation to the City Council regarding the
  Commission’s assignments in FY 2024-2025.

  Public Safety Director Duefias provided an overview of the agenda report and
  presented a recommended list of assignments, including a few consolidations from
  last year's list.

  Commissioner Merrick inquired whether an item on parking education could be
  added to the list of recommended assignments.

  Public Safety Director Duefias recommended “To provide feedback about parking
  program education”

  There was consensus amongst the Public Safety Commission to include this item
  on the list of recommended assignments.

  Public Works Director shared that he visited Portugal, and they have an app that
  notifies people where they can park.

  Commissioner Gibbs inquired about including a specific item on PCH safety issue
  tracking.

  Public Safety Director Duefias stated that the first item on the list is a catch—all and
  PCH falls under number one, which gives commissioners flexibility to add things
  to the agenda.

  Vice Chair Speigle inquired regarding changing the word in number nine regarding
  the tow yard from “search” to recommend. There was consensus amongst the
  Public Safety Commission.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of May l, 2024
Page 5 of 9

MOTION  Commissioner Merrick moved and Vice Chair Spiegel seconded a motion to
  approve the list of public safety recommended assignments with the change
  regarding the addition of “To provide feedback about parking program education”
  and changing the word “search” to “make recommendations for permanent
  locations for impound site.” for the number nine regarding the tow yard. The
  question was called and the motion carried 4—0, with Commissioner Anneet
  absent.

  B. Homeless Services Report

  Recommended Action: Discuss recent homeless services activities and receive
  and file the monthly reports for January and February 2024 from The People
  Concern.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores provided an overview of the agenda report and
  presented an update on homeless outreach efforts. He provided a preliminary
  report on the homeless count numbers of 51 which has been one of the lowest
  counts since they begun the homeless count. He went over the numbers of people
  getting placed into permanent housing in West Los Angeles. He added that the
  People Concern has done great work in the City of Malibu.

  Chair Frost inquired regarding the Zuma Creek encampment.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores stated that HOST, Beaches and Harbors, and the
  Sheriffs Department are involved and it is in the process of being cleared out
  SOOI'l.

  Commissioner Merrick inquired if the better numbers are due to more housing or
  fewer homeless people.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores stated that results are due to many reasons, including
  a new housing facility that just opened up, interim shelter, and additional outreach
  opportunities.

  Chair Frost inquired regarding the availability of the Santa Monica shelter.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores stated that this location is full however, motel
  vouchers could be provided.

  Vice Chair Spiegle inquired if numbers are down countywide.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores stated that information is not out yet for the county,
  however, stated that the City of Malibu has lower numbers than other cities.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of May l, 2024
Page 6 0f 9

  Public Safety DirectOr Duenas stated that the ratio of outreach to homeless
  numbers are higher in the City of Malibu than other areas. She stated that constant
  contact and getting to know the community makes a difference.

  Vice Chair Spiegle stated that momentum and consistency are important.

  Public Safety Director Duefias stated that the Public Safety Commission will now
  get a monthly report.

  Chair Frost commended the work of the Public Safety team on their efforts to get
  people housed.

  Commissioner Gibbs commended the work of the Public Safety Department.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores stated that they have made significant strides and
  there is much work to do.

  The Public Safety Commission received and filed this report.

  C. Impound Site Update

  Recommended Action: l) Receive a report from staff on the status of a summer
  impound site, and 2) Discuss options for a year-round, day-use impound site.

  Public Safety Director Duefias presented the staff report and opened up the
  discussion for a year-round site.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores this year's temporary impound yard will be at Malibu
  High School for the summer. He stated that we do not pay the school and this is a
  joint partnership.

  Public Safety Director Dueflas reminded the commission of zoning limits on
  certain sites, however, stated that zoning amendments could be explored. She
  recommended that the commission keep in mind proximity, availability, access,
  and regulations such as ESHA.

  Sergeant Soderlund stated that the temporary impound yard gets an average daily
  use of about 15-20 cars.

  Vice Chair Spiegle inquired if the city would be working with private CSO’s this
  year again.

  Public Safety Director Duenas stated that the goal is to begin by the Fourth of July
  holiday.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of May l, 2024
Page 7 of 9

  Chair Frost opened public comment.

  Moshe Ben Dayan spoke about his towing business and requested that a Malibu
  tow yard include a temporary office and restroom. He spoke about the importance
  of needing a tow yard in Malibu. He stated that a 150 ft by 50 ft lot will stow 20—
  30 cars comfortably. He added that these locations are temporary and not meant to
  store vehicles for more than 48 hours.

  Chair Frost closed public comment.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores stated that the Heathercliff lot is 160 ft by 130 ft,
  which could flt 65 cars.

  Chair Frost stated that enforcement is needed to write 180’s.

  Commissioner Gibbs stated the bottleneck would fall under CSOs.

  Sergeant Soderlund stated that the current system has a one-hour wait time for a
  180 and stated that it takes up time from deputies.

  Chair Frost recommended the top of the chili cook-off lot.

  Public Safety Director Duefras stated that a zoning amendment would be needed to
  allow for towing.

  Vice Chair Spiegle added that his goal was to have a temporary year-round site.

  Commissioner Gibbs stated that currently there is an outreach project to gather
  public input for city-owned community lands.

  Sergeant Soderlund stated that the majority of parking issues are around Zuma,
  Point Dume, and the Malibu Pier.

  Chair Frost opened public comment.

  Hans Laetz inquired if the Public Safety Commission intends to make a decision
  on what to do with the community lands.

  Chair Frost closed public comment.

  Chair Frost stated that this is a temporary permanent solution and stated that space
  is needed for tows to address public safety concerns.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes 0f May l, 2024
Page 8 of 9

  Commissioner Merrick agreed and stated that the use of the space could be
  modified later.

  Vice Chair Spiegle stated that the La Paz lot would be difficult to use.

  Vice Chair Spiegle inquired about using the La Paz or Triangle Lot.

  Public Safety Director Duenas stated that permits would be needed.

  Chair Frost recommended that the Public Safety Commission recommend a
  portion of the Chili Cook—Off lot.

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry reminded the commission of the weather conditions
  in that area.

  Chair Frost inquired about using base and gravel.

  Public Works Director DuBouX stated that permits will be needed.

  Vice Chair Spiegle spoke about the importance of having a year—round temporary
  permanent tow yard.

MOTION  Commissioner Merrick moved and Chair Frost seconded a motion to recommend
  a portion of the chili cook-off site not to exceed 20,000 sq of a 9.5 acre site, to be
  used as a temporary year—round tow yard. The question was called and the motion
  carried 4-0, with Commissioner Anneet absent.

  D. Public Safetv Agency Activity

  Recommended Action: Discuss recent Public Safety Agency activities and receive
  and file activity reports from the County of Los Angeles Sheriff’s Department,
  Fire Department, Lifeguard Division, and the California Highway Patrol.

  Sergeant Soderlund presented crime statistics for the month of April 2024. He
  discussed a theft that occurred and reminded the community not to leave valuable
  items in their cars. He discussed traffic safety efforts which yielded several DUI
  stops, speed citations, and reckless driving. He added that there were several
  arrests for narcotics and paraphernalia. He stated that Lost Hills Station now has
  two new motors, Sean Gervais and Mike Kelly. He stated that Lost Hills Sheriff
  Station will be having an open house on June 1, 2024, and invited the community
  to attend.

  Malibu VOP Team Leader Russo presented parking enforcement statistics for the
  month of April 2024. He stated that much of the need is in Winding Way, Point
 Malibu Public Safety Commission

  Dume, Zuma, and Broad Beach. He stated that they are always trying to recruit
  new members and added that currently, they have 19 members. He explained that
  it would be helpful to have a consistent state parks staff at Point Dume.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 6:57 p.m., Commissioner Merrick moved, and Chair Frost seconded a motion
  to adjourn the meeting. The question was called and the motion carried 4—0, with
  Commissioner Anneet absent.

  Approved and adopted by the Public Safety Commission of the
  City of Malibu on August 7, 2024.
